items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: The guys who pioneered like Lester Young and Coleman Hawkins and all that kind, they know all that sort of stuff.

ctx.x: PS: Did you have any foresight or a moment of clairvoyancy where you saw him becoming one of the master saxophonists in jazz history? Do you think, did you recognize his talent -

No, I didn't. Now that's, I'll answer that with no strings, I didn't. I didn't ever think he would be that great, you know. But I'll tell you one thing, though, he was conscientious, he studied. He - the lesson was always, he did what I told him to do. I mean, for - 'cause I had a whole lot of people, 65 or 70, and when I had, some kid that come in, give me the money in front and "Mr. Waters, so on and so on and so on", pay me in front, and go for 3 and 4 weeks and don't even look at the lesson. 'Cause I know, I…
PS: When did you figure out that you were gonna leave the Boston area, what was your thinking behind that and what made you go back to the Philadelphia area briefly?
